Use Beanie ODM built on Motor (async) as the prompt requested

decision: I chose to read DOCUMENTDB_URI from an environment variable and include .env.example with placeholders.

Read connection string from environment variable DOCUMENTDB_URI at runtime
reason: This follows the run environment guidance and security best practices to avoid committing secrets.
evidence: Readiness report: 'The connection string is in the environment variable DOCUMENTDB_URI. Read it from the environment at run time. Never write its value into a file.'

decision: I chose NOT to provision any Azure resources programmatically; the sample will use the existing cluster described in the run environment and will provide IaC files as examples only if necessary.
alternatives: Provision Azure DocumentDB cluster via az/bicep from sample
Do not provision resources; use existing cluster and document instructions
reason: Policy forbids resource creation; using the existing cluster avoids unnecessary actions and matches environment assumptions.

decision: I chose to make OpenAI optional and fall back to a deterministic local extractor/embedding when OPENAI_API_KEY is not set; the code will use OPENAI if provided.
alternatives: Use OpenAI (hosted) for LLM and embeddings by default
Use local deterministic fallback when OPENAI_API_KEY missing
reason: This ensures the sample can be run without external API keys for verification while supporting real LLMs if keys are available.
evidence: Assumption from prompt review: 'Builder will use a hosted LLM + embedding provider (commonly OpenAI)... make configurable via env.' Also enrich/enrich.py contains this pattern already.

decision: I chose text-embedding-3-small (1536 dimensions) as the default embedding model, configurable via OPENAI_MODEL_EMBEDDING and EMBEDDING_DIMENSIONS environment variables.
alternatives: Use OpenAI text-embedding-3-small (1536 dims)
Use a different embedding provider/dimension
reason: text-embedding-3-small is a compact, commonly available embedding model; matching dimensions is important for creating the native vector index. Making it configurable allows users to change provider or dims.
evidence: Common choice and the code's default: OPENAI_EMBEDDING_MODEL env default 'text-embedding-3-small' and EMBEDDING_DIMENSIONS default '1536' in enrich/enrich.py.

decision: I chose to escape braces in the f-string prompt by doubling them so the JSON appears verbatim in the injected prompt string.
alternatives: Leave the OpenAI prompt as-is and risk syntax error
Escape braces in the f-string to produce literal JSON in the prompt
reason: To produce a valid Python string that contains literal JSON braces in an f-string, braces must be doubled. This is a minimal code change to restore functionality.
evidence: enrich/enrich.py raised SyntaxError due to unescaped braces inside an f-string.

decision: I chose to add src/__init__.py to make it an importable package, keeping the simple top-level script entrypoints unchanged.
alternatives: Run scripts with PYTHONPATH set or change imports to relative
Make src a package by adding __init__.py
reason: Adding __init__.py is a minimal change to allow 'from src.db import init_db' to work across scripts and is a common repo layout practice.
evidence: ModuleNotFoundError: No module named 'src' when running enrich/enrich.py.

decision: I chose to append the repository root to sys.path at the top of scripts to ensure 'src' imports work when running scripts directly, which is a minimal local-dev convenience change for samples.
alternatives: Modify all scripts to use package install (pip)
Temporarily append repo root to sys.path in scripts for simplicity
reason: Keeps scripts runnable directly without requiring users to install the package; acceptable for a sample repo.
evidence: ModuleNotFoundError persisted after adding src/__init__.py; inserting repo root into sys.path is a standard fix for scripts.

decision: I chose to update src/models.py to use Beanie's current recommended Settings class (set name = 'survey_responses') and remove the deprecated Collection inner class.
alternatives: Keep deprecated Collection inner class and accept Beanie deprecation error
Update models.py to use Settings class per Beanie 1.24 requirements
reason: Fixing the model to current Beanie API ensures init_beanie succeeds and the sample works with the pinned package versions.
evidence: Runtime beanie.exceptions.Deprecation: 'Collection inner class is not supported more. Please use Settings instead.'

decision: I chose to call client.close() without await at the end of enrich_all, because AsyncIOMotorClient.close() is synchronous and not awaitable.
alternatives: Call await client.close() for Motor client
Call client.close() without await since AsyncIOMotorClient.close() is synchronous
reason: Calling client.close() synchronously prevents the TypeError and correctly closes sockets.
evidence: TypeError: object NoneType can't be used in 'await' expression when attempting to await client.close(). The Motor client close() is synchronous per Motor docs.

decision: I chose to create a vector-diskann index on 'embedding' with dimensions=1536 and similarity='COS' via the documentdb MCP create_index API.
alternatives: Create native vector-diskann index on embedding
Skip creating vector index
reason: Enables efficient vector search matching the sample embedding dims.
evidence: documentdb-vector-search skill guidance: 'Create a vector-diskann index with correct dimensions, similarity.'

decision: I chose to stop retrying the MCP create_index call after it failed and record the failure; the sample will document the expected vector index and leave manual creation via portal/CLI as fallback.
alternatives: Retry different API payloads until success
Stop and record that MCP create_index failed and require manual portal/CLI index creation
reason: Repeated tool failures indicate either permissions, API mismatch, or server-side restriction; per builder guidance stop after second attempt and take alternate route to avoid causing side effects or infinite retries.
evidence: documentdb_create_index tool returned an error twice with vague 'Function failed' message when attempting to create a vector index.
